description:
FOUND s508 (Fable, 2026-10-05) by the review probes for s507c PART ONE; PRE-EXISTING on main fee16466, same answers on the s507c tree (its #2690 gives a REQUIRED file its own unit boundary; the eval text and the do-file do not have one yet).

REPRODUCERS (probe names in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s508/review/ph.pl (IMPL TAG [REGEX]; answers in out/ph.perl / ph.base / ph.tree; perl 5.40.3, main fee16466, the s507c tree 0229e0ec)):
  ev-unit-run  UNITCHECK { print "u\n" } print "run1\n"; eval q{UNITCHECK { print "eu1\n" } UNITCHECK { print "eu2\n" } print "ebody\n"}; print "run2\n";
               perl: u / run1 / eu2 / eu1 / ebody / run2            PCL: u / run1 / ebody / run2            (the two blocks never run)
  ev-run       ... eval q{CHECK {..} INIT {..} UNITCHECK { print "eu\n" } BEGIN { print "eb\n" } END { print "ee\n" } print "ebody\n"; 1} ...
               perl: c / run1 / eb / eu / ebody / run2 / ee         PCL: the same without `eu`
  ev-begin     CHECK { print "c\n" } BEGIN { eval q{CHECK { print "ec\n" } UNITCHECK { print "eu\n" } INIT { print "ei\n" } print "ebody\n"; 1} } INIT { print "i\n" } print "run\n";
               perl: eu / ebody / ec / c / ei / i / run             PCL: ebody / eu / ec / c / ei / i / run  (UNITCHECK after the body)
  do-file      CHECK { print "c\n" } BEGIN { do "./f.pl" } print "run\n"; do "./f.pl";   with f.pl = CHECK / UNITCHECK / INIT / BEGIN blocks + a body
               perl: f:b / f:u / f:body / f:c / c / f:i / run / f:b / f:u / f:body / end   PCL: f:b / f:body / f:u / ... / f:b / f:body / end  (late at BEGIN time, absent at run time)
  mod-eval-in  a module whose load-time code does `eval q{UNITCHECK { print "M2:eu\n" } ...}`: perl prints M2:eu between M2:body and M2:after; PCL (run 2) never.

WHAT PERL DOES: UNITCHECK blocks run right after the compilation UNIT that holds them is compiled, last-defined first, before that unit's first run-time statement -- for the main program, for a required file, for a do-file and for every string eval.  CHECK and INIT blocks in a unit compiled at run time are "too late to run" (already right in PCL); in a unit compiled while the main program compiles they join the program's queues (right for a required file since #2690, and right for these two as probed above).

DESIGN POINTER: s507c's `%p-load-unit` / `*p-unit-load*` (ir-spec 9.0a) IS the mechanism -- give the eval text and the do-file the same unit boundary: fresh UNITCHECK queue, drained after the unit's compile-phase forms and before its body.  The measurement to take first: does an eval's emitted text have a point "after its compile-phase forms, before its first run-time form" today (a module's file does: its own `(p-run-compile-phase-blocks)`)?


=== s507c (s509): NOT done ===
Not started in s507c; the unit machinery it needs (%p-load-unit, the UNITCHECK drain at a unit boundary, ir-spec §9.0a) is on main since the PART ONE merge.
subject: A UNITCHECK block in an `eval STRING` or a `do FILE` never runs when the eval / do runs at RUN time, and runs AFTER the unit's body (not right after its compile) when it runs at BEGIN time -- the eval text and a do-file are compilation UNITS like a required file (#2690)
